drivingQuestion: How may several women bake matza in one oven?

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים לָשׁוֹת כְּאַחַת וְאוֹפוֹת בְּתַנּוּר אֶחָד, זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «Rabban Gamliel says: Three women may knead» their dough «as one,» meaning at one time, «and bake» the batches of dough «in one oven, one after the other,» and they need not be concerned that their dough will become leavened while they are waiting to use the oven.

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים עוֹסְקוֹת בְּבָצֵק כְּאַחַת, אַחַת לָשָׁה, וְאַחַת עוֹרֶכֶת, וְאַחַת אוֹפָה.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis say: Three women» may be «engaged» in preparing «dough as one,» in the following manner: «One kneads» her dough as another «one arranges» her own dough so it takes the form of matza, while another «one bakes» her dough.

segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים וְלֹא כׇּל הָעֵצִים וְלֹא כׇּל הַתַּנּוּרִים שָׁוִין. זֶה הַכְּלָל: תָּפַח — תִּלְטוֹשׁ בְּצוֹנֵן.
segments.en: «Rabbi Akiva says: Not all women, not all wood, and not all ovens are the same,» and therefore no set rules should be established. Rather, «this is the principle:» If the dough begins to «rise, she» should «spread cold» water in which she immersed her hands, onto the dough, in order to stop the leavening process.
